The [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] monitors the length of hospital stays for acute surgery patients across Denmark. This comparison analyzes the statistical distribution of these stays—measured in days via minimum, first quartile (Q1), median, and third quartile (Q3)—for all Danish regions and individual hospitals during the 2023–2024 period [^src1].

Rigshospitalet is the clear leader in terms of the longest hospital stays, recording a median of 18.00 days and a Q3 of 43.00 days [^src1]. This Q3 value is a massive outlier, more than double the national Q3 of 17.00 days [^src1]. Sygehus Lillebælt and Aarhus Universitetshospital also report extended stays, with medians of 13.00 and 11.00 days, respectively [^src1]. On the other end of the spectrum, Bispebjerg og Frederiksberg Hospital reports the shortest stays, with a median of just 6.00 days and a Q3 of 11.00 days [^src1]. Herlev og Gentofte Hospital and Sygehus Sønderjylland follow closely with medians of 7.00 days [^src1]. The national median for Denmark sits at 8.00 days [^src1].

Regarding minimum stays, the vast majority of regions and hospitals report a minimum of 0.00 days [^src1]. However, Sygehus Lillebælt, Aarhus Universitetshospital, and Regionshospitalet Randers stand out as outliers by recording a minimum stay of 1.00 day [^src1].

While the source document's summary mentions longitudinal trends—specifically an increase in Rigshospitalet's median from 18 to 22 days and a change in Aalborg Universitetshospital's Q3 from 22 to 16 days (which the summary text describes as a "markant stigning" or significant increase, despite the numerical decrease) when comparing 2023–2024 to 2024–2025—this specific comparison dataset only contains the single 2023–2024 table [^src1]. Therefore, these multi-year trends cannot be independently verified across multiple dated sections within this view.
